items.rationale: Provide a platform-neutral, upstream-owned lazy composition seam that validates complete profile selections before constructing only the selected protocol groups, handlers, location services, integrations, and built-in tools.
Move desktop Global path directory creation from module import to Global service-layer construction so replacement profiles can inject HAP-private paths without eager writes to desktop XDG locations.

Import the lightweight LocationServiceMap service tag directly so server middleware can consume an injected location graph without eagerly importing the desktop aggregate containing watcher, PTY, PluginInternal, Npm, and other unselected leaves.

Split executable legacy configuration, runtime-installed Provider packages, bundled Provider selection, and prompt selection behind upstream-owned modules so portable profiles can retain upstream Config/Provider/AI SDK semantics without importing the desktop plugin, npm, native-LLM, location-service, or unrestricted dynamic-loading graphs.

Remove two unused Session imports that eagerly pull the complete V2 location-service, PTY, native watcher, and plugin graph, and split executable external tool loading behind an upstream-owned module so portable profiles can retain the upstream stable Session state machine without opaque runtime imports.

Split the platform-neutral plugin definition helper and watcher event contract into lightweight upstream-owned leaves so the stable Session graph can preserve upstream skill and file-tool semantics without eagerly importing runtime npm installation, dynamic plugin execution, observability exporters, or native watcher implementations.

Place the optional TypeScript-backed Code Mode interpreter behind a lightweight upstream-owned loader so portable profiles can keep the authoritative ToolRegistry while explicitly withholding an interpreter whose opaque runtime module loading cannot be included in the deterministic Harmony bundle.

Expose the existing upstream ModelsDev service as a configurable layer so portable profiles can inject a private cache, packaged snapshot, bounded refresh limits, and fixed source while retaining upstream Provider normalization and custom configuration semantics.

Lock the existing upstream global configuration, instance disposal, Provider reconstruction, model-limit override, and invalid-payload preservation semantics with a cross-platform regression without adding Harmony-owned Provider behavior.

Keep upstream AI SDK and Session error classification intact while replacing raw Provider error logging, which can retain prompts, echoed credentials, and endpoint secrets, with bounded cross-platform diagnostics. Add a real OpenAI-compatible 401 transport regression and redaction coverage without introducing Harmony-specific Provider behavior.

Lock the existing upstream Session authority to stable identifiers, CRUD, multi-turn context, tool continuation, compaction, retry retirement, event ordering, instance reconstruction, and read-only recovery without mutation replay. Explicitly inject the portable location-service layer into focused tests without changing Session production behavior.

items.rationale: Invalidate upstream instance-scoped Provider state synchronously after the authoritative Auth service sets or removes credentials, so the next request cannot race against cached Provider keys. Lock the real typed HTTP routes, global disposal event, and secret-free response with a cross-platform regression.
crossPlatformTests: packages/opencode/test/server/httpapi-auth.test.ts -t invalidates Provider instance state after setting and removing credentials

items.rationale: Place only the built-in ToolRegistry selection and ordering behind a platform-neutral module so embedded profiles can select a strict capability subset while retaining upstream tool names, schemas, permissions, results, and Session lifecycle behavior; the default implementation preserves the complete desktop selection.

Move stable built-in definition loading and its desktop process/native service nodes behind one platform-neutral boundary. The default loader preserves desktop behavior, while embedded profiles can omit unsupported definitions and their eager dependencies without cloning upstream names, schemas, permissions, results, or Session lifecycle behavior.

Route only the accepted upstream workspace tool definitions through a replaceable, narrowly scoped filesystem service. The desktop default delegates to FSUtil, while embedded profiles can enforce an authorized project root, stale mutation preconditions, atomic writes, and changed-path reporting without restricting application-private configuration or cloning official tool schemas and results.

Keep explicitly marked migrated tool parts available to history APIs and generic client rendering while excluding them from later Provider model requests. This is a platform-neutral display-only history contract; it neither recognizes Harmony-private tool names nor registers a compatibility tool.

Sort filesystem matches within each configured discovery root, load them sequentially to preserve declared precedence for duplicate names, and return the final skill set by name. Commands derived from Skill.all therefore have stable order across filesystems and restarts without changing configuration scope precedence.

Separate public HttpApi middleware tags, routing query schemas, Provider response schemas, and portable handler factories from their live desktop composition while preserving the existing exports and desktop layers. Route construction can then consume the authoritative upstream contract and handler logic without eagerly loading Provider plugins, workspace proxying, runtime package installation, PTY, or unrelated native services.

Add a versioned platform-capability extension to the existing experimental capabilities route, derive structured 501 responses from the same immutable gate snapshot, inject that provider into portable handlers, and expose the same response and error types through the generated official SDK. The extension records acceptance gates only and deliberately does not duplicate live Provider, MCP, LSP, session, or connection resource state.

Move the public MCP resource schema into a process-free upstream module and make the experimental route consume that module directly. Desktop MCP re-exports the same schema, while Harmony route construction no longer has to load the stdio-capable MCP service merely to describe its official response.

Extend the upstream generated-client contract suite with explicit Provider, nested model, agent, MCP status, permission, tool definition, cancellation, and versioned capability operations. This closes the previously implicit portions of the Tier-A SDK matrix without adding a Harmony-only client or test server.

Allow the existing upstream route composition to receive the versioned platform-capability provider while preserving the desktop default, and exercise structured unavailable results through the real generated SDK and HttpApi service graph. The seam avoids a Harmony-only dispatcher and makes unsupported-route behavior a cross-platform upstream contract.

Consume the versioned platform capability profile in the upstream SolidJS client and fail closed before terminal, worktree, MCP, LSP, plugin, or external-process queries and mutations. Unavailable controls are disabled or replaced with an explicit bounded explanation, background capability refresh retains the last accepted description, and worktree/process submission guards run before session creation or busy-state mutation.

Allow a portable server bootstrap to select explicit global paths, force every instance route onto one host-authorized project, inject already-reviewed platform service replacements into the upstream application graph, and retain the upstream listener, route, Session, Provider, event, and generated-SDK authorities.

Retain the upstream MCP service, Streamable HTTP and SSE transports, catalog, tool conversion, authentication, reconnect, notification, and disposal semantics while isolating the unavailable local stdio process transport behind an explicit fail-closed result.
Allow the upstream SolidJS MCP surface when the accepted remote MCP capability is present while continuing to ignore and fail closed for the independently unavailable local stdio MCP transport.

Factor the existing upstream MCP HttpApi handlers over an injected instance API so portable compositions can select the MCP group without importing the desktop aggregate that also owns PTY and TUI routes.

Synthesize valid custom OpenAI-compatible provider entries and fallback model descriptors so custom providers configured through auth or config are retained in the provider catalog and do not fail with ModelNotFoundError.

sharedPatches.acceptance: No shared patch may be applied or packaged unless every required field is present and the checksum matches. Platform-only changes belong in Harmony-owned roots.
